title: help and manifest do not tell a first-time caller how to write a valid task create
description:
A session reading only `quest help <command>` and `quest manifest --json` cannot reliably write a valid `task create` on the first try. Reported by opum-web (three consecutive "task create received invalid arguments" failures before `quest instructions task-creation` gave the right form), reproduced by the orchestrator, and reproduced again here against source at 74bbe1d. I hit it myself earlier the same day: my first call was `task create --title "shape probe"`, which failed, and my next move was `help task create | head -40`, which did not show me the answer.

ONE CORRECTION to the report, because it changes the fix. It is not true that nothing says the title is positional. `help task create` DOES print:

    summary: Create a task.
    usage: quest task create "<title>" --actor <name> --actor-kind human [--priority High] [--type bug]

on lines 53 and 54 of 56. The defect is placement, not absence: those two lines sit underneath ~50 lines of alphabetized `fields:` and `flags:` names, so anything that truncates (a pager, `head`, a context-budgeted agent read, a narrow terminal) sees only the machine dump. `usage` is the single most useful line in the output and it is last. The three genuine gaps:

1. ORDERING. `summary` and `usage` print after the full fields/flags dump. They should lead. This is the whole fix for the positional-argument half and it is nearly free.

2. VALUE FORMAT IS UNDOCUMENTED PER FLAG. Neither the flag list nor `usage` says which flags take a JSON array in one pass (`--acceptance-criteria '["a","b"]'`, `--plan`, `--definition-of-done`, `--implementation-notes`), which are repeatable scalars (`--label`, `--doc`, `--dependency`), or which need structured objects (`--comments` wants `{id, authorId, body, createdAt}`). `help task edit`'s summary documents the `--comments` shape in prose; `help task create` documents none of it. The flag list is a list of names, and a name does not carry arity. QCLI-250 made a JSON-array-shaped value a usage error for the repeatable-scalar flags, which is the right behaviour but only tells you after you get it wrong.

3. `manifest --json` CONFLATES DOMAIN FIELDS WITH FLAGS. `task create`'s entry is `{name, schemaVersion, kind, mutates, fields[]}`, and `fields` lists `title` and `acceptanceCriteria` alongside `priority` and `type` with nothing distinguishing them. `title` is positional, not settable by `--title` at all; `acceptanceCriteria` maps to `--acceptance-criteria` taking a JSON array. A caller generating a command line from the manifest -- which is what a manifest is for -- writes `--title` and fails. There is no arity, no positional marker, no value kind.

QCLI-127 is the predecessor and is Done: it stopped `help` from being a raw manifest echo and added `summary`/`usage`/`details`. This is the unfinished half of that -- the prose exists but is placed where a truncating reader never reaches it, and it does not cover value formats.

The acceptance test the orchestrator set is the right one and is what makes this checkable rather than cosmetic: a session reading ONLY help and the manifest writes a valid create on the first try. Worth testing with the first 20 lines of help output rather than all 56, since truncation is the actual failure mode.

Not urgent, no release of its own; it stacks with whatever pair ships next.

acceptanceCriteria.text: quest help <command> prints summary and usage BEFORE the fields and flags lists, so a reader truncating the output still sees the positional form
Flag documentation states each flag's value shape: JSON array in one pass, repeatable scalar, or structured object -- not just the flag name
quest manifest --json distinguishes positional arguments from flags and states each entry's value kind, so a caller generating a command line from the manifest does not write --title
A test drives a valid task create built only from the first 20 lines of quest help task create plus quest manifest --json, with no reference to quest instructions

plan: 1. Sweep manifest/help consumers in two passes BEFORE designing (done): nothing reads commands[].fields; lore-cli verifyManifest tolerates unknown keys. Therefore the manifest change is additive -- fields[] stays byte-identical and new keys sit alongside it.

2. Single source of truth for parameter shape: lift the per-command repeatable-flag lists and the booleanFlags set out of main.ts inline literals into an exported table, and declare the JSON-array flags there too. Both help and manifest read that table, so the two surfaces cannot disagree with each other or with the parser.

3. Ordering: renderHumanPayload takes an optional priority-key list; the help path passes summary and usage so they print above the fields/flags dump. Generic rendering for every other payload is unchanged and still alphabetical.
4. Help flags carry their value shape in the rendered string (--acceptance-criteria <json-array>, --label <string, repeatable>), since help is explicitly the human surface (QCLI-127).

5. Manifest gains parameters: {positional: [...], flags: {<flag>: {value, repeatable}}} additively, so a caller generating a command line knows title is positional and --acceptance-criteria takes one JSON array.

6. The acceptance test: build a valid task create from the FIRST 20 LINES of quest help task create plus quest manifest --json, with no reference to quest instructions, and run it. Twenty lines, not all 56, because truncation is the failure mode.
7. bun run check green, land on dev behind PR. No release; it stacks.
implementationNotes: Predecessor: QCLI-127 (Done) stopped quest help echoing the raw manifest and introduced summary/usage/details. This is its unfinished half -- the prose landed at the bottom of the machine dump rather than above it, and never covered per-flag value shapes. Related: QCLI-250 (Done) made a JSON-array-shaped value a usage error on the repeatable-scalar flags, which is correct but only informs a caller after the failure; this task is about informing them before.

Consumer sweep for the manifest schema change, run BEFORE the change per the orchestrator's condition, using the two-pass method recorded in CLAUDE.md.

PASS 1, bare field names on the manifest/help payload. Pattern: [."'[]<field>\b for fields, flags, filters, usage, summary, commands across opum-cli-e2e suites/lib/bin, lore-cli/src and opum-fleet/hooks. Counts 22/38/4/49/39/17; every hit on a quest payload read.

PASS 2, command invocation. Pattern: "manifest" | quest manifest | manifest --json, plus "help" and help.commands. This is the pass that finds consumers who never name a field.

RESULT: nothing reads commands[].fields anywhere in the fleet. The real manifest consumers are opum-cli-e2e 10-contract-quest.mjs:35-56 (reads commands[].kind and asserts it is dotted command.payload form, plus a non-empty count) and 20-quest-discovery.mjs:129 (finds the entry named 'version' and checks the command is invocable). Help consumers read data.commands length and name only -- 20-quest-discovery.mjs:88-100. lore-cli's verifyManifest (src/adapters/quest.ts:649-662) checks name, schemaVersion, kind and mutates on its REQUIRED_COMMANDS and ignores everything else; it is NOT a strict schema and tolerates unknown keys.

CONCLUSION: an ADDITIVE manifest change -- new keys alongside the existing ones, with fields[] left exactly as it is -- breaks nothing in the fleet and needs no coordination. A change that reshaped fields[] entries from strings to objects WOULD be breaking, which is why this task takes the additive route. That is the sweep deciding the design rather than just clearing it.
